editorial_intro: Happy 4th of July weekend! The multiplex is stacked: Minions & Monsters just stormed in with the franchise's best reviews ever, Toy Story 5 refuses to slow down past $325M, and today's big diaspora drop is Alpha — Alia Bhatt and Sharvari go full spy mode in YRF's first female-led Spy Universe film. Obsession is now streamable but still filling seats (94% RT — earned it). Looking ahead: July is about to get nuclear with Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey on the 17th, Dhamaal 4 bringing the chaos on the 10th, and Spider-Man closing out the month. Summer doesn't get bigger than this.

movies.title: Toy Story 5
movies.why_watch: Two weeks in and already past $325M domestic — Pixar made the toys fight an iPad and somehow it works. Jessie finally gets her movie, Taylor Swift wrote the end-credits ballad, and yes, you will cry. The family event of the summer, no question.

movies.title: Minions & Monsters
movies.why_watch: The Minions go to Hollywood, accidentally unleash monsters, and critics are calling it the franchise's best film — a love letter to classic cinema that's genuinely witty for adults while keeping kids in stitches. 93% on RT is no joke for a Minions movie.

movies.title: Alpha
movies.why_watch: YRF's Spy Universe gets its first female-led entry, and Alia goes full assassin. Early word: Bobby Deol dominates, Sharvari holds her own, and Hrithik's cameo as Agent Kabir is a whistle-worthy moment. Not the franchise's best, but the action sequences are grand and it's a legit event for diaspora theaters this weekend.

movies.title: Obsession
movies.why_watch: Made for $750K, grossed $370M+, and Spielberg himself said he loved it. A monkey's-paw horror that's equal parts funny and deeply disturbing. Now on VOD too, but the theater experience — hearing a packed crowd scream — is irreplaceable. The breakout of 2026.

movies.title: Disclosure Day
movies.why_watch: Spielberg's first summer blockbuster in 8 years is a government-conspiracy alien thriller with Emily Blunt delivering what critics call the best performance of her career. Not peak Spielberg, but his worst is still better than most directors' best. Oscar buzz for Blunt is real.

movies.title: Supergirl
movies.why_watch: Critics are split and the box office stumbled, but Milly Alcock's raw, whiskey-soaked Kara Zor-El is genuinely great — and Jason Momoa's Lobo is a riot. If you liked the grittier DC tone, this cosmic road trip is better than the 55% RT suggests. Audiences rate it 76%.

movies.title: Moana (Live-Action)
movies.why_watch: Disney brings the ocean to life — literally — with a live-action Moana. Dwayne Johnson is back as Maui, and the visuals promise to be jaw-dropping. Whether Disney's live-action machine can recapture the animated magic is the question, but this one's a safe family bet.

movies.title: Dhamaal 4
movies.why_watch: The boys are back for another round of unhinged slapstick treasure-hunting. You already know what you're getting — leave your brain at the door and laugh for two hours. The original gang reuniting is the selling point, and diaspora theaters will be rowdy. Perfect popcorn Bollywood.

movies.title: The Invite
movies.why_watch: A24 assembles a murderer's row cast — Rogen, Wilde, Cruz, Norton — for what promises to be the kind of sharp, uncomfortable ensemble comedy-drama they do best. Details are scarce, but that cast list alone earns a ticket.

movies.title: Evil Dead Burn
movies.why_watch: The Deadites return in what's being pitched as the most vicious Evil Dead yet — a grief-soaked woman trapped with her in-laws as they turn one by one. If it hits anywhere near Evil Dead Rise's level, horror fans are in for a gnarly ride.

movies.title: The Odyssey
movies.why_watch: Christopher Nolan adapts Homer's Odyssey, shot on IMAX, with the most stacked ensemble of the year. After Oppenheimer swept the Oscars, this is the most anticipated film of 2026 — and it's already breaking pre-sale records. This is the one you see in the biggest, loudest theater you can find.

movies.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
movies.why_watch: Tom Holland swings back years after No Way Home's devastating ending — Peter Parker isolated, targeted by multiple villains, and undergoing a mysterious mutation. The most anticipated Marvel movie since Endgame. July 31 can't come fast enough.
